chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The one who visits his brother for the Sake of Allah, not for anything else, seeking the Promise of Allah and accomplishing what is in the Presence of Allah, Allah would allocate seventy thousand Angels calling out to him: 'Indeed! You have done well, and the Paradise is (Made to be) better for you'.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting a brother for the sake of Allah?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to underscore that Ziyarat al-Akhi (visiting a brother) is an act of pure devotion (Ikhlas) rather than social obligation. The invocation of seventy thousand angels signifies the immense divine honor bestowed upon the visitor, affirming that such visits are a tangible means of securing Allah's promise and realizing the spiritual presence of the Divine. This tradition is foundational in Shia ethics for strengthening communal bonds through spiritual intent.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who visits his brother for the Sake of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> not for anything else, seeking the Promise of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> and accomplishing what is in the Presence of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Allocate seventy thousand Angels calling out to him: ‘Indeed! You have done well, and the Paradise is (Made to be) better for you’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn Faddal from Ali ibn ‘Aqaba from abu Hamza from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Whoever visits his brother (in belief) for the sake of Allah and for no other reason, seeking thereby the promise of Allah, and to achieve what is with Allah, Allah will appoint seventy thousand angels who applaud, ‘How beautiful is what you have done and how beautiful is paradise (for you).”’
